A.lost: The price leverage against the incumbent, and the months of re-qualification discovered only when the switch is finally attempted and the second line is gone.

B.lost: The team that goes when the cut is actually made, and the product if it does not survive their going, on a state the company had never stood in.

C.lost: The lead's trust and the round with it, the day the named sheet is checked and found not to exist.

D.lost: Quarters of the company's plans and numbers handed to a party reading it for free, never recalled and never seen on any ledger.

E.lost: The estate's remaining value, sold at the floor to the horse chosen because it would win, with the fee paid on top.

F.lost: The terms offered on reputation alone, gone the day a down market or a rival's check updates the counterparty's model and the holder is found to hold nothing.

G.lost: The fund drained to zero with nothing won, and the members' wages for every week it took to learn the employer could outlast the meter.

H.lost: Every deadline this party will ever name, discounted from the moment the counterparty saw it still seated after the date.

I.lost: The second source's willingness to quote, gone after it learned it was the stalking horse, and the price leverage that went with it.

J.lost: The appeal above the lord, and with it every dispute afterward decided at the lord's own table once the crown stops needing the town.

K.lost: Every future constraint this party names, read as a choice from the day it found the money it said it did not have.

L.lost: The seller's standing in the venue and its exposure to prosecution, once a lot the ringer won reappears in the next sale.

M.lost: The case itself, when the funder withdraws below its threshold and the plaintiff cannot pay the distance to trial.

N.lost: The terms folded on in the last hour, and the counterparty's new knowledge that this party has no floor.

O.lost: The price the refusal was holding up, once the lead learns the alternative is the insiders' bridge and reads it as the outsiders' absence.

P.lost: A season's sales or a strike's wages spent to keep the record, or the record itself if the party folds when tested.

Q.lost: The company liquidated or the founder gone to keep the threat real, or the threat itself forever once the counterparty called it and the holder folded.

R.lost: The private table, ended the moment the letter goes out, and the one shot itself if the crowd turns out smaller than the counterparty feared.
